answer_text:
Let \(A\) be a \(300\times 300\) real matrix satisfying \(A=A^{-1}\). Then

\[
A^2=I.
\]

Since the polynomial \(x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)\) has distinct roots, every such \(A\) is diagonalizable over \(\mathbb{R}\) with eigenvalues \(1\) and \(-1\).

Suppose \(A\) has \(k\) eigenvalues equal to \(1\), and \(300-k\) eigenvalues equal to \(-1\). Then for some invertible matrix \(S\),

\[
A=S\begin{pmatrix}I_k&0\\0&-I_{300-k}\end{pmatrix}S^{-1}.
\]

For fixed \(k\), the number of independent real parameters is the dimension of the conjugacy orbit:

\[
\dim GL_{300}(\mathbb{R})-\dim\left(\text{centralizer of }\begin{pmatrix}I_k&0\\0&-I_{300-k}\end{pmatrix}\right).
\]

Now,

\[
\dim GL_{300}(\mathbb{R})=300^2=90000.
\]

A matrix commuting with

\[
\begin{pmatrix}I_k&0\\0&-I_{300-k}\end{pmatrix}
\]

must be block diagonal of the form

\[
\begin{pmatrix}B&0\\0&C\end{pmatrix},
\]

where \(B\) is \(k\times k\) and \(C\) is \((300-k)\times(300-k)\). Thus the centralizer has dimension

\[
k^2+(300-k)^2.
\]

So the number of free real parameters for fixed \(k\) is

\[
90000-\bigl(k^2+(300-k)^2\bigr)=2k(300-k).
\]

We maximize this over \(k=0,1,\dots,300\). The quadratic \(2k(300-k)\) is maximized at

\[
k=150,
\]

giving

\[
2\cdot 150\cdot 150=45000.
\]

Thus the largest family of such matrices has \(45000\) real degrees of freedom, and no smaller number of real variables can describe all of them.

\[
\boxed{45000}
\]
